verified_key_information_units.information: Consolidated revenue decreased 2.6% to EUR 765.3 million (from EUR 785.8 million in 2024), with core route operations down EUR 13.7 million to EUR 625.2 million; EBITDA declined to EUR 130.1 million (from EUR 175.2 million); net profit fell to EUR 17.3 million (from EUR 40.3 million) with earnings per share at EUR 0.02 (from EUR 0.05).

candidate_sentences.text: The Group’s consolidated revenue decreased by 2.6% year-on-year to EUR 765.3 million, down from EUR 785.8 million in 2024.
This contraction was primarily attributed to a drop in route operations revenue, which fell by EUR 13.7 million to EUR 625.2 million.
EBITDA declined by EUR 45.1 million, or 25.7%, to EUR 130.1 million from EUR 175.2 million in 2024.
Consequently, the audited net profit for the period dropped by 57.1% to EUR 17.3 million, compared to EUR 40.3 million in the prior year.
Earnings per share fell to EUR 0.023 from EUR 0.054.

verified_key_information_units.information: Passenger volumes decreased 0.9% to 5.5 million (from 5.58 million in 2024); cargo units transported fell 19.2% to 245,004 (from 303,234); passenger vehicles carried declined 2.2% to 760,473 (from 777,592).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report: 'Key Figures' table and operational summary stating passenger, cargo, and vehicle volumes for 2025 vs 2024.

candidate_sentences.text: Operational metrics reflected this weakness, with the number of passengers carried decreasing by 0.9% to 5.5 million and cargo units transported falling sharply by 19.2% to 245,004.
Passenger vehicle numbers also declined by 2.2% to 760,473.

verified_key_information_units.information: Key performance drivers included weak consumer and business confidence, geopolitical tensions impacting demand; fleet optimization through vessel sales and continued chartering; cost efficiency measures; and a depreciation expense decline from aligning cruise/passenger vessel useful lives to 45 years (excluding shuttle vessels).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report: 'The following operational factors impacted...' section and 'Earnings' section detailing depreciation impact and strategic focus on cost efficiencies.

candidate_sentences.text: AS Tallink Grupp reported a challenging financial year in 2025, characterized by a decline in revenue and profitability driven by subdued consumer confidence and geopolitical tensions in its core Baltic markets.
A key positive factor was the alignment of the estimated useful lives of cruise and passenger vessels to 45 years, which reduced depreciation expense by EUR 18.0 million to EUR 79.8 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Fleet management involved the sale of three vessels (passenger vessel Star I in April, cargo vessels Regal Star in August and Sailor in October) and reduction of lay-up vessels from four to zero by Q3 2025; three vessels (Romantika, Galaxy I, Silja Europa) remained chartered out at year-end.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report: Bullet points under operational factors listing vessel sales, lay-up reductions, and chartering details.

candidate_sentences.text: The Group also completed the sale of three vessels, generating proceeds of EUR 78.8 million and helping to optimize the fleet.
The Group continued to focus on cost efficiency and optimized capacity, chartering out three vessels to generate additional revenue.

verified_key_information_units.information: Segment performance: Estonia-Finland route revenue increased EUR 1.7 million to EUR 314.5 million (passenger volumes up 1.8%) while Finland-Sweden routes declined EUR 3.3 million to EUR 225.5 million (due to maintenance) and Estonia-Sweden routes fell EUR 12.1 million to EUR 85.3 million (passenger volumes down 12.5%).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report: 'Sales and Segments' section breaking down revenue and results by route, including passenger/cargo unit changes and maintenance impacts.

verified_key_information_units.information: Net debt decreased to EUR 432.4 million (from EUR 537.7 million in 2024) with a net debt/EBITDA ratio of 3.3 (vs 3.1 in 2024); cash position impacted by EUR 44.6 million dividends paid (plus EUR 11.3 million related income tax) and EUR 113.5 million in loan repayments and interest during the year.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report: 'Liquidity and Cash Flow' section detailing net debt, dividend payments, and financing activities.

verified_key_information_units.information: Strategic focus on emissions reduction includes preparations to transition shuttle vessels (MyStar and Megastar) to liquified biomethane from 2026, targeting a 75% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions and cost mitigation amid regulatory pressures.

details.completeness_justification: The candidate summary adequately covers the core material meaning of K1 (revenue, EBITDA, net profit, EPS), K2 (passenger volumes, cargo units, passenger vehicles), K3 (weak consumer/business confidence, geopolitical tensions, fleet optimization, cost efficiency, depreciation expense decline), K4 (sale of three vessels, fleet optimization), K5 (segment performance for Estonia-Finland, Finland-Sweden, Estonia-Sweden routes), K6 (net debt decrease, net debt/EBITDA ratio), and K8 (emissions reduction strategy for shuttle vessels). However, it omits the specific details for K7 (capital investments totaling EUR 33.0 million for vessel maintenance and IT systems, and planned maintenance/repair works of 73 vessel-days) and K9 (post-reporting-period management changes including Paavo Nõgene's resignation, Peep Jalakas' appointment, and Margus Schults' removal from the Management Board). These omissions are material because they concern specific financial planning and corporate governance developments. The overall coverage is strong but not complete, justifying a score of 3 (Generally yes).
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is fully coherent internally. All statements are logically connected, with consistent explanations for revenue declines, profitability metrics, and strategic actions. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, or organizational problems. The summary flows logically from overall performance to specific metrics, causes, and strategic responses. While there are multiple negative trends reported (revenue decline, passenger/cargo decreases, profit drops), these are consistently attributed to the same underlying causes (subdued consumer confidence, geopolitical tensions) without contradiction. The positive elements (asset management, vessel sales, fleet optimization) are presented as counterbalancing factors without conflicting with the overall negative trend. The structure moves coherently from performance overview to financial metrics to operational details to strategic actions.
